How to play

Roll, buy, build, collect rent

If you've ever played a property trading game at the kitchen table, you already know how Pixonomy works. Go round the board, buy the cities you land on, finish a colour set, build on it, and charge everyone who lands there. The last player with money wins.

  1. Roll 01

    Throw two dice and move. Doubles roll again; a third double in a row sends you to the Lockup.

  2. Buy 02

    Land on a city nobody owns and buy it, or let it go to auction, where everyone can bid.

  3. Build 03

    Own a whole colour set, build houses evenly across it, then hotels. Rent climbs with every one.

  4. Bankrupt 04

    Trade, mortgage and haggle to stay afloat while your rivals run out of cash. Last tycoon standing wins.

Features

The classic loop, with more ways to win (and to backstab)

Everything you expect from a dice-and-deeds board game is here. On top of it, Pixonomy adds real deal-making and a stack of optional house rules that keep game night from playing out the same way twice.

Real deals

Trading

Put anything on the deal slip and haggle until someone signs.

  • Cities, cash and Bail Passes
  • Promises: rent-free visits, IOUs, rent shares
  • Counter-offers, up to three rounds

Auctions

Bidding

Pass on a city and the whole table bids for it. Bargains, bidding wars and bluffs.

  • On by default
  • Everyone bids, even the player who passed
  • Your cash is your limit

Houses, hotels

Building

Build up your sets and watch the rent climb. Landmarks go one step further.

  • 32 houses and 12 hotels for the whole table
  • Hoard houses and nobody else can build
  • Optional landmarks on top

Ability cards

House rule

Every Payday, take one of two ability cards or $100 instead.

  • 12 cards, Common to Epic
  • Hold up to three
  • Play them before or after you roll

Chaos Mode

House rule

Every round opens with an event that shakes up the whole table.

  • Market Crash: rent halved
  • Property Boom: rent up 50%
  • Tax Holiday, and seven more

Secret missions

House rule

A hidden goal only you can see. Finish it for a payout, then get the next.

  • Up to three a game
  • Kept secret online too
  • A reason to make that odd trade

Teams

House rule

Play 2 v 2 or 3 v 3. Teammates share colour sets for rent and building.

  • Split a set with your partner
  • Turns alternate between teams
  • Great with four or six

Underdog rules

House rule

Comebacks happen. Rules that help whoever's behind, so nobody gets bored and quits.

  • A bounty on the leader's rent
  • Double or nothing on big rent
  • Catch-up cards for last place

FAQ

Questions

What kind of game is Pixonomy?

Pixonomy is a property trading board game in pixel art. You roll two dice, move round a board of 36 tiles, buy the cities you land on, complete colour sets, build houses and hotels, and collect rent from everyone who lands on your property. Trade, bid at auctions and bluff your way to the top: the last player with money wins.

Can I play Pixonomy online with friends?

Yes. Invite your Steam friends to play online, host a game on your local network (LAN), or share one PC and pass the mouse or controller round. You can fill any empty seat with a CPU player.

How many players can play?

2 to 6 players, in any mix of people and computer players.

Can I play alone against the computer?

Yes. CPU rivals come in Easy, Normal and Hard, and they trade, bid at auctions and build just like people do. There's also a daily challenge with the same dice and cards for every player.

If I know the classic property board game, will I know how to play?

Yes. Roll, buy, build, collect rent and bankrupt your rivals: the core loop is the one you know from the kitchen table. Pixonomy adds a deal slip with promises and IOUs, auctions, a Bank Loan corner, the Lucky Spin, ability cards, Chaos Mode, secret missions, teams and underdog rules, all of which you can switch on or off.

How long does a game take?

You choose. Set a round limit and the richest player wins when the rounds run out, pick the Quick preset for a short game, or play the classic way until only one player is left.

Does Pixonomy have house rules like auctions and a jackpot?

Yes. Auctions and even building are on by default. You can also set the starting cash, a round limit, a turn timer and a jackpot that pays out on the Lucky Spin, turn on teams, ability cards and Chaos Mode, or add extra ways to win by sets, cash or railroads.

Can I play Pixonomy for free?

Yes. A free prototype is on itch.io right now, so you can roll the dice and buy your first city today. The full game is coming to Steam.

Which platforms is Pixonomy on?

Pixonomy is coming to Steam for Windows PC. You can play with a mouse, a keyboard or a controller.

When does Pixonomy come out?

Pixonomy is in development and has no release date yet. Wishlist it on Steam and Steam will tell you the day it comes out; until then, the free prototype is on itch.io.
